response.passage: In the city of Graph-Land, a treasure hunter named Rohan is using a map to find hidden gold. The map is a Cartesian plane where the origin (0,0) is the central Town Square. Rohan starts at the origin and moves to plot his first point at (-2, 3). He knows that the x-coordinate represents his horizontal distance from the center, so he moves 2 units to the left and 3 units up. He marks this spot clearly. Next, he needs to plot a point on the y-axis to mark a bridge. He knows that for any point on the y-axis, the x-coordinate must be 0, so he marks (0, 5). Rohan notices that the map grid uses a scale where each square represents 10 meters, showing that axes do not always have to count by ones. He draws a straight line connecting his points to represent a path. He extends this line beyond his plotted points, knowing that a linear relation continues infinitely in both directions. Finally, he checks his position in the second quadrant, which is the top-left section of the map. He is careful not to confuse this with the other quadrants, which are numbered in a counter-clockwise direction starting from the top-right.
response.summary: Rohan uses a Cartesian coordinate system to navigate a map and find treasure. He correctly applies rules for plotting points, understanding axes, and drawing linear paths.
